_captured: 2026-10-17 (post-migration capture; supersedes the pre-migration capture the same day)
_source: docs/backend/baseline-audit.sql run read-only in the Supabase SQL editor of the deployed HALO project
_contents: catalog only: table and column definitions, RLS flags, policies, foreign keys, functions, privileges, triggers, extensions, roles. No rows from any HALO table, no passwords, no keys.
_findings: server_version_num 170006 = PostgreSQL 17.6. The local test suite runs on PGlite/Postgres 18.
Migrations 0001 to 0018 are all applied. 17 public tables, including operations (0017) and recovery_challenges (0018).

0015 fully applied AND validated: save_household present; symptom_logs carries band, entry_date, note_length, symptoms_count and severity checks, every one validated true; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE are revoked from anon and authenticated on profiles, household_bands, symptom_logs and notification_prefs, with the select-own policies still in place as designed.

0016 fully applied: home_contexts with its three checks, both unique keys, the one-current partial unique index, daily_scores.home_context_id, the composite foreign key to home_contexts(profile_id, id) with no action on delete, and transition_home_context plus update_home_context_attributes granted to service_role only.

0017 and 0018 fully applied and closed: operations has its 5 checks, recovery_challenges its 7, both have RLS enabled with NO policies, and both grant anon and authenticated NOTHING (empty privilege lists). The revoke lines did what they were written for.

FINDING, latent privilege: anon and authenticated hold TRUNCATE, REFERENCES and TRIGGER on every table in public, from Supabase's default privileges. Row level security does NOT govern TRUNCATE, so unlike the leftover INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grants on the other tables, this one is not inert. Proved locally: an authenticated role is denied 'delete from public.symptom_logs' and yet allowed 'truncate public.symptom_logs', which would empty every household's journal. NOT reachable through the deployed surface: PostgREST has no TRUNCATE verb, and the only functions anon and authenticated may execute (handle_new_user, rls_auto_enable) return trigger types Postgres refuses to call directly. REMEDIATED 2026-10-17: the YOUR_TODO 2.7 revoke was applied to production, so neither role holds TRUNCATE, REFERENCES or TRIGGER on any public table any more. The block is tested in test/migrationBackout.test.mjs. This capture predates that remedy, so its table_grants show the privileges still present.

The local reconstruction matches the deployed catalog on every table-grant line checked (operations, recovery_challenges, profiles, symptom_logs, household_bands, notification_prefs, home_contexts, alerts) and on the set of 17 table names, so the PGlite test suite is not resting on a schema production does not have.

ucmr5_utilities has RLS enabled with a single SELECT policy named 'Allow public read access on ucmr5_utilities' using (true). The anon/authenticated INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grants are inert under RLS. The guarded remedy in YOUR_TODO 1.1 was NOT needed and was NOT run.
The reconstruction had guessed that policy's name as 'Enable read access for all users'; no deployed policy ever had that name. Corrected in reconstructed_baseline.sql and in the YOUR_TODO remedy.

supabase_migrations_ledger is null: migrations are applied by hand in the SQL editor, so no ledger rows exist. That 0001-0018 are applied is inferred from schema shape, not recorded. The state query in YOUR_TODO 2.6 is how to check.

STILL UNEXPLAINED: production carries a SECURITY DEFINER function rls_auto_enable() returning event_trigger with search_path=pg_catalog, with EXECUTE granted to anon and authenticated. It is in no migration, no baseline and not in the local reconstruction. It cannot be called directly (Postgres refuses to invoke an event trigger function), and the audit does not read pg_event_trigger, so whether an event trigger is bound to it is still unknown. Worth finding out what created it.
map_layers and water_snapshots have RLS enabled with no policies at all: service-role-only tables.

handle_new_user is SECURITY DEFINER with EXECUTE granted to anon and authenticated. It returns trigger so it cannot be called directly. The on_auth_user_created trigger on auth.users is present and enabled.
auth.users carries email and email_confirmed_at, which is what GET /api/account reads to report a linked recovery method. The column the B02 code depends on exists as assumed.

Extensions: pgcrypto 1.3, vector 0.8.2, uuid-ossp 1.1, pg_stat_statements 1.11, supabase_vault 0.3.1. Default privileges still grant arwdDxtm on new public tables to anon and authenticated for both the postgres and supabase_admin owners, which is why every new migration must revoke explicitly.
_note: The full catalog JSON was reviewed in the session transcript rather than stored here, because it names every column of every table and is reproducible at any time by re-running docs/backend/baseline-audit.sql. For a quick answer on which migrations are applied, use the state query in docs/backend/YOUR_TODO.md 2.6.
